content: Adverse reactions to terbinafine have been observed in both clinical trials and post-marketing experiences. Below is a detailed description of these reactions: 1. Clinical Trials Experience: Adverse reactions reported during clinical trials include gastrointestinal symptoms such as diarrhea, dyspepsia, and abdominal pain. Abnormalities in liver function tests have been noted. Dermatological reactions such as rashes, urticaria, and pruritus were observed. Taste disturbances, including changes in taste perception, were reported. Changes in the ocular lens and retina were documented, although the clinical significance of these findings remains unclear. Most adverse events were mild, transient, and did not necessitate discontinuation of the study drug. 2. Post-Marketing Experience: Allergic Reactions: Cases of angioedema and severe allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported. Autoimmune Disorders: Terbinafine has been associated with the precipitation or exacerbation of cutaneous and systemic lupus erythematosus, as well as serum sickness-like reactions. Psychiatric Disorders: Anxiety and depressive symptoms, independent of taste disturbances, have been reported. In some cases, depressive symptoms resolved upon discontinuation of therapy but recurred with re-initiation. Nervous System Disorders: Taste disturbances, including complete loss of taste, have been reported. These disturbances can be severe enough to cause reduced food intake, weight loss, anxiety, and depressive symptoms. Smell disturbances, including loss of smell, have also been documented. Cases of paresthesia and hypoesthesia have been reported. Eye Disorders: Visual field defects and reduced visual acuity have been observed. Ear and Labyrinth Disorders: Hearing impairment, vertigo, and tinnitus have been reported. Vascular Disorders: Vasculitis has been documented. Gastrointestinal Disorders: Pancreatitis and vomiting have been reported. Hepatobiliary Disorders: Cases of liver failure, some leading to liver transplantation or death, have been reported. These include idiosyncratic and symptomatic hepatic injury, hepatitis, cholestasis, and elevated hepatic enzymes. Skin and Subcutaneous Tissue Disorders: Serious skin reactions, including acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, psoriasis-like eruptions or exacerbation of psoriasis, photosensitivity reactions, and hair loss, have been reported. Musculoskeletal and Connective Tissue Disorders: Rhabdomyolysis, arthralgia, and myalgia have been observed. General Disorders and Administration Site Conditions: Malaise, fatigue, influenza-like illness, and fever (pyrexia) have been reported. Investigations: Altered prothrombin time (both prolongation and reduction) in patients treated concomitantly with warfarin, as well as increased blood creatine phosphokinase levels, have been reported. These adverse events highlight the importance of monitoring patients on terbinafine therapy, particularly for serious or rare reactions.
